subtitle: From Kamarupa’s hills to Gauda’s fallen capital, a king signs his name into history

panels.shot: sweeping low-angle wide of a royal camp outside a distant city, under a darkening sky
panels.action: Bhaskaravarman stands on a raised earthen platform in a vast camp of tents, ships’ masts rising beyond a riverbank and lines of elephants and horses arrayed before the walled city of Karnasuvarna on the horizon.

dialogue.text: In a camp outside fallen Karnasuvarna, bachelor-king Bhaskaravarman lifts not his sword, but a copper plate, to show that Kamarupa’s voice now reaches Bengal and Kanauj.

i18n.hi: गिरे हुए कर्णसुवर्ण के बाहर शिविर में, कुंवारा-राजा भास्करवर्मन तलवार नहीं, ताम्रपत्र उठाता है, दिखाने कि कामरूप की आवाज़ अब बंगाल और कन्नौज तक गूँजती है।

panels.shot: slow push-in from high aerial over the Brahmaputra valley towards a misty hill-fort
panels.action: A bird’s-eye view of the lush Brahmaputra valley cradling a hilltop capital in Kamarupa, with Bhaskaravarman shown small, standing on the ramparts, gazing westward over forests and distant ridges.

dialogue.text: Kamarupa’s hills kept their own rhythm, far from the battles of the Ganga plains, yet from these misty ramparts a young king watched the west with careful eyes.

i18n.hi: कामरूप की पहाड़ियाँ गंगा के मैदानी युद्धों से दूर अपनी ही ताल पर थीं, पर इन्हीं धुंधीले किलों से एक तरुण राजा सतर्क नज़र से पश्चिम को देखता रहा।

panels.shot: medium close-up on Bhaskaravarman seated in court, scrolls and priests around him
panels.action: Bhaskaravarman sits on a simple yet dignified throne, Brahmana scholars unrolling palm-leaf manuscripts before him as a court poet recites his ancient Varman lineage.

dialogue.text: The Nidhanpur plates later trace his line to the Varmans of Kamarupa, yet the scholar’s eye warns us: genealogy on copper is praise as much as it is memory.

i18n.hi: निधनपुर के ताम्रपत्र उसे कामरूप के वर्मनों से जोड़ते हैं, पर विद्वान चेताते हैं: ताम्रपत्र की वंशावली उतनी ही स्तुति है, जितनी याद।

panels.shot: wide shot of a map-like tableau showing three regions with emblematic icons
panels.action: A stylised landscape shows Kamarupa’s hills with an elephant standard, Gauda’s flat delta with a lion banner, and Kanauj’s central plain with a royal umbrella, with faint routes of trade and messengers between them.

dialogue.text: To his west, Shashanka ruled Gauda from Karnasuvarna; further beyond, Harsha rose at Kanauj. Between hills, rivers and rice plains, each king watched the others’ moves in wary silence.

i18n.hi: उसके पश्चिम में शशांक कर्णसुवर्ण से गौड़ पर राज करता था; उससे आगे कन्नौज में हर्ष उठ रहा था। पहाड़, नदियाँ और धान के मैदानों के बीच, हर राजा चुपचाप दूसरे की चालें तौल रहा था।

panels.shot: intimate interior shot, low light, Bhaskaravarman reading a letter by lamplight
panels.action: In a dim chamber, Bhaskaravarman holds a finely written birch-bark letter, the lamplight catching his thoughtful face, while a trusted scribe waits silently beside him.

dialogue.text: Banabhatta’s Harshacharita sings of letters, gifts and meetings between Bhaskaravarman and Harsha, but his pen flatters his master; behind the poetry, we glimpse only the outline of their diplomacy.

i18n.hi: बाणभट्ट का हर्षचरित भास्करवर्मन और हर्ष के पत्रों, उपहारों, मुलाक़ातों का गान करता है, पर उसका कलम अपने स्वामी की चापलूसी करता है; कविता के पीछे हमें बस उनकी कूटनीति की आहट मिलती है।

panels.shot: medium wide of a war council tent, map spread on low table
panels.action: Bhaskaravarman leans over a cloth map marked with stones and small wooden elephants and ships, surrounded by generals and Brahmana advisers in a large tent filled with the muffled sounds of a camp.

dialogue.text: What we know is this: by the time his Nidhanpur charter was issued, Bhaskaravarman had brought his camp to Karnasuvarna, Shashanka’s old capital. How he reached there, the record leaves unsaid.

i18n.hi: इतना तो पक्का है: जब तक उसका निधनपुर ताम्रपत्र निकला, भास्करवर्मन अपना शिविर शशांक की पुरानी राजधानी कर्णसुवर्ण तक ले आया था। वह वहाँ कैसे पहुँचा, लेख चुप है।

panels.shot: dynamic tracking shot along a column of marching troops
panels.action: A long column of Kamarupa soldiers, elephants with tower-howdahs, cavalry and infantry moves along a riverbank, with Bhaskaravarman riding at the head beneath a simple canopy, the distant outline of Bengal’s flatlands ahead.

dialogue.text: His copperplates call it a victorious camp, filled with ships, elephants, horses and foot-soldiers—a king of the eastern hills now marching into the low, wide lands of Gauda.

i18n.hi: उसके ताम्रपत्र इसे विजयी शिविर कहते हैं, जहाज़ों, हाथियों, घोड़ों और पैदल सिपाहियों से भरा—पूरब की पहाड़ियों का राजा अब गौड़ की नीची, चौड़ी धरती पर कूच कर चुका था।

panels.shot: wide river-level shot of a fleet and army moving together
panels.action: On a broad river, boats with raised prows and warriors glide downstream, keeping pace with elephants and cavalry on the bank, while Bhaskaravarman stands at the prow of the lead vessel, cloak whipping in the wind.

dialogue.text: The inscription’s proud list of ships hints at more than land war; river routes carried men and grain, and Kamarupa’s king learned to move with both water and earth beneath him.

i18n.hi: शिलालेख में जहाज़ों की शान से भरी गिनती बताती है कि यह सिर्फ़ ज़मीन की लड़ाई नहीं थी; नदियों पर ही लोग और अन्न चलते, और कामरूप का राजा पानी और मिट्टी दोनों पर चलना सीख चुका था।

panels.shot: tense medium shot at the outskirts of a city, hazy walls in background
panels.action: Bhaskaravarman pauses with his commanders on a raised mound, looking towards the distant walls and spires of Karnasuvarna through the morning haze, the army halted behind him in expectant silence.

dialogue.text: And then, Karnasuvarna—the city of Gauda—lay before him. Whether taken by assault, yielded in fear, or emptied by Shashanka’s own end, the sources do not say.

i18n.hi: और फिर, कर्णसुवर्ण—गौड़ की नगरी—उसके सामने थी। आक्रमण से टूटी, डर से छोड़ी, या शशांक के अंत से सूनी—किसी स्रोत ने साफ़ नहीं लिखा।

panels.shot: wide shot inside Karnasuvarna’s streets, with Kamarupa troops entering
panels.action: Kamarupa soldiers and elephants move cautiously through a broad street of Karnasuvarna, its markets shuttered and citizens watching from doorways, as Bhaskaravarman rides slowly under the shadow of once-royal towers.

dialogue.text: We only know this: the bachelor king of distant Kamarupa now held his camp in the heart of Gauda’s former capital, a presence as political as it was military.

i18n.hi: हम इतना ही जानते हैं: दूर के कामरूप का कुंवारा राजा अब गौड़ की पुरानी राजधानी के दिल में शिविर डाले बैठा था—उतना ही राजनीतिक डेरा, जितना सैनिक।

panels.shot: interior wide of a captured palace hall now turned into a camp office
panels.action: Inside a large hall with worn yet ornate pillars, Bhaskaravarman sits at a low desk amid rolled copper plates, scribes and officials, the open doorway framing a glimpse of the bustling camp outside.

dialogue.text: Here, in this repurposed hall of Karnasuvarna, he chose his next weapon: not spear or chariot, but a copperplate grant that would carry his name from Assam’s hills to Bengal’s fields.

i18n.hi: यहीं, कर्णसुवर्ण की बदले हुए सभा में, उसने अगला हथियार चुना: न भाला, न रथ, बल्कि ताम्रपत्र का दान, जो उसका नाम असम की पहाड़ियों से बंगाल के खेतों तक ले जाएगा।

panels.shot: close-up on Bhaskaravarman dictating to a scribe
panels.action: Bhaskaravarman leans forward, eyes steady, as he dictates to a seated scribe who scratches carefully on a waxed board, a blank copper plate resting ready beside him.

dialogue.text: “Write: from our victorious camp at Karnasuvarna, we grant…”

i18n.hi: "लिखो: हमारे विजयी कर्णसुवर्ण शिविर से, हम यह अनुग्रह देते हैं…"

panels.shot: extreme close-up of stylus on copper, hand and plate filling the frame
panels.action: A scribe’s hand incises neat Nagari characters into the shining surface of the copper plate, the phrase about the victorious camp and its ships, elephants, horses and foot-soldiers partially visible.

dialogue.text: The Nidhanpur inscription fixes the moment: a camp described as victorious, furnished with ships, elephants, horses, foot-soldiers, and a Kamarupa king issuing land charters in the heart of Gauda.

i18n.hi: निधनपुर का शिलालेख उस घड़ी को बाँध देता है: शिविर विजयी कहा गया, जहाज़ों, हाथियों, घोड़ों, पैदल सिपाहियों से सजा, और कामरूप का राजा गौड़ के बीचोंबीच भूमि-दान जारी कर रहा है।

panels.shot: medium shot of Bhaskaravarman handing the plate to Brahmana donees
panels.action: Bhaskaravarman stands as a group of Brahmana recipients bow before him; he extends the finished copperplate toward their leader, who reaches out with both hands in solemn acceptance.

dialogue.text: The plate records the grant of lands to Brahmanas, carrying his authority into fields and villages; in rewarding allies, he also plants legal anchors for Kamarupa’s reach in eastern Bengal.

i18n.hi: ताम्रपत्र ब्राह्मणों को दी गई ज़मीन दर्ज करता है, उसकी सत्ता को खेतों और गाँवों तक बिखेरता; मित्रों को पुरस्कृत करते हुए वह पूर्वी बंगाल में कामरूप की पहुँच के कानूनी खूंटे गाड़ता है।

panels.shot: wide shot of rural Bengal landscape where the grant applies
panels.action: A peaceful scene of ploughed fields, palm trees and a village in eastern Bengal, with a local headman showing the copperplate to gathered villagers as farmers pause from their work to listen.

dialogue.text: Far from Karnasuvarna’s walls, those plates meant new rights, obligations and overlords. For villagers, the king was a name on metal; for historians, that metal is proof of his eastern shadow.

i18n.hi: कर्णसुवर्ण की दीवारों से दूर, उन ताम्रपत्रों का मतलब था नए हक़, नए फ़र्ज़, नए स्वामी। गाँववालों के लिए राजा बस धातु पर लिखा नाम; इतिहासकारों के लिए वही धातु उसके पूर्वी साए का सबूत।

panels.shot: intercut shot showing Bhaskaravarman and Harsha in their own courts, separated by frame
panels.action: A split composition shows Bhaskaravarman on one side in his eastern court, and Harsha on the other in Kanauj, each seated on a throne, courtiers around them, a faint imagined line of messengers connecting the two spaces.

dialogue.text: Bana would later praise gifts and courtesies between Bhaskaravarman and Harsha, an eastern alliance written in elegant prose; yet even he cannot tell us exactly how Shashanka’s space was unmade.

i18n.hi: बाण बाद में भास्करवर्मन और हर्ष के उपहारों और शिष्टाचार की पूर्वी मित्रता को सजधज कर लिखता है; पर वह भी साफ़ नहीं कह पाता कि शशांक की ज़मीन कैसे दरक गई।

panels.shot: medium close-up of Bhaskaravarman alone at dusk in the camp, thoughtful
panels.action: As dusk falls over the Karnasuvarna camp, Bhaskaravarman stands alone near a tent rope, watching the flicker of distant fires, the copperplate resting on a low table beside him.

panels.shot: wide, slightly elevated shot of the camp being slowly dismantled at dawn
panels.action: At dawn, soldiers fold tents and lead elephants away from Karnasuvarna, boats pushed off the riverbank, while Bhaskaravarman prepares to mount his horse, the city’s silhouette receding behind him.

dialogue.text: He did not remake Gauda into Kamarupa; no source claims he ruled Bengal for long. The camp at Karnasuvarna was a moment, not a permanent conquest.

i18n.hi: उसने गौड़ को कामरूप नहीं बना दिया; कोई स्रोत नहीं कहता कि उसने बंगाल पर देर तक राज किया। कर्णसुवर्ण का शिविर एक पल था, स्थायी विजय नहीं।

panels.shot: modern-museum-style shot of the Nidhanpur plate on a dark background, ghostly overlay of Bhaskaravarman behind
panels.action: The Nidhanpur copperplate lies displayed against a dark backdrop, its script catching the light; behind it looms a faint, respectful image of Bhaskaravarman, half in shadow, half in glow.

dialogue.text: Today, the Nidhanpur plate speaks more clearly than any poet: for a brief, sharp season, Bhaskaravarman carried Kamarupa’s seal to Karnasuvarna, proving that a king’s most lasting victories may be written, not fought.

i18n.hi: आज निधनपुर का ताम्रपत्र किसी कवि से ज़्यादा साफ़ बोलता है: थोड़े, तीखे समय के लिए भास्करवर्मन कामरूप की मुहर लेकर कर्णसुवर्ण पहुँचा, दिखाते हुए कि राजा की सबसे टिकाऊ जीतें तलवार नहीं, लिखाई से भी होती हैं।

subtitle_i18n.en: From Kamarupa’s hills to Gauda’s fallen capital, a king signs his name into history
subtitle_i18n.hi: कामरूप की पहाड़ियों से गिरे गौड़ की राजधानी तक, एक राजा अपना नाम इतिहास में लिखता है
